claim: An impasse in Soar is raised by a fixed architectural rule applied to the preference outcome (empty set after reject, all candidates beaten, unresolved tie, no new operator), not by the system judging its own progress.
agent_test: Compare code-fired triggers (no pass, same error twice, no change after 2 rounds) against a model-stated 'I am stuck' trigger at equal tokens on a fixed item set; count wasted rounds and missed stalls.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The count of impasse types is not canonical: Laird 2022 main text says 3 (state no-change, operator tie/conflict, operator no-change), Laird 2022 glossary and Manual 9.6 say 4 (tie, conflict, constraint-failure, no-change), and splitting no-change gives 5. Constraint-failure is absent from the Laird 2022 main text.
agent_test: None needed. Design choice: type our impasses by what our checks can detect, not by Soar's count.

claim: Soar tie and conflict impasses can always be removed by adding preferences, but constraint-failure (several require, or require plus prohibit on one value) cannot be resolved by more preferences. Laird 2022 footnote 4 states the universal claim; Manual 9.6 limits it to tie and conflict. The Manual wording is more specific and is taken as correct.
agent_test: Seed contradictory hard constraints (two required answers) in a test set; check the scaffold reaches the fallback (best attempt so far, G6) instead of looping.

claim: When a tie or conflict and a constraint-failure occur together, Soar detects only the constraint-failure, so hard constraints are handled before preference evaluation.
agent_test: In S6 run the hard-constraint check before any ranking or operator choice; compare loops with and without that ordering.

claim: A Soar substate is isolated: it reads the superstate, runs its own decision cycle and preference memory, and returns only results; non-result substate data is deleted. Returned results are justified by the superstate elements they needed.
agent_test: Run subgoals in a fresh context that returns one typed result line, versus a shared growing context, at equal tokens; measure anchoring on earlier failed attempts.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In Soar, chunking maps impasse type to learned rule type: state no-change gives operator-proposal rules; tie or conflict gives evaluation (search-control) rules; operator no-change gives application rules.
agent_test: After a solved subgoal store a typed note (what failed, which operator fixed it) keyed by impasse type and retrieve it on the next same-type impasse; compare with no memory at equal tokens. Deeper study belongs to the chunking subfield.

claim: Operator no-change is ambiguous: it fires both when knowledge is missing and when an external action simply takes several cycles. Soar needs extra rules to tell the cases apart. Any LLM stall detector inherits this ambiguity.
agent_test: Log stalls fired by 'same error twice' and label by hand whether the item was truly stuck or slow tool output; report precision.

claim: Soar offers time-bounded substate reasoning: when time is short a non-optimal or random decision is taken. This fallback is stated but not specified or measured in any source opened.
agent_test: Compare a hard token cap on subgoal depth with best-attempt fallback against no cap, at equal total tokens.

claim: Impasse-time LLM calls that are compiled into reusable rules cut later LLM use. CogRec reports LLM-call frequency falling to a low plateau only with chunking (figure only). Zhu and Simmons report a bootstrapped agent solving find 15/15 with 12/15 needing no LLM call, and query tokens of about 917 against 54,754 for an action-only LLM agent (table scrambled in extraction). Mohan et al. 2012 turn grounding failures into instructor queries and learn from few examples.
agent_test: Within a stream of similar items, cache validated fixes from subgoals and reuse them; measure tokens per item against re-deriving each time, at equal accuracy.

claim: Accuracy gain from impasse-triggered LLM queries is small in the only benchmarked case. CogRec HR@10 on MovieLens-1M is 0.3124 against LLM-Direct 0.2901 (+7.7% relative) and best baseline GPT4Rec 0.2956 (+5.7%); gains over the best baseline across all 12 columns are 4.1 to 9.1%. No seeds, variance or significance tests; results not split by impasse type.
agent_test: Do not expect large accuracy gains from impasse typing alone; test accuracy and token cost together.

claim: Most raw LLM answers are not usable by a grounded agent (over 70% unviable on tidy kitchen, 58% groceries, 85% office). Checking and repairing them with the agent's own knowledge is what lifts completion; widening the candidate tree alone gives no gain (kitchen 52.5 to 50.0, office 35.7 to 21.4).
agent_test: Add an external grounded check plus one repair step to candidate generation and compare with more sampling alone at equal tokens.

claim: STARS-style analyse, repair and select raises task completion without human help (kitchen 52.5 to 77.5, groceries 66.7 to 94.4, office 35.7 to 92.9) at about 3.4x, 3.6x and 5.9x the baseline tokens (139,871 vs 41,407; 61,808 vs 17,078; 76,056 vs 12,992). No equal-token control such as best-of-N; the main table is one run per condition, and 10 runs exist only for STARS (means 77.5, 93.89, 92.14; SD 2.04 for kitchen).
agent_test: Run best-of-N with the same grounded check at the STARS token budget; the difference is what repair adds.

claim: Reasoning without external feedback does not self-correct: GPT-3.5 after two self-correction rounds fell on GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8, HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0; earlier gains used an oracle stopping signal. Checks grounded in an executor or the agent's own knowledge do help (NL2GenSym critic ablation, STARS analysis and repair).
agent_test: Compare S5 revision that cites code-located failing output against revision from the model's own opinion, at equal tokens.

claim: An execution-grounded critic is the most valuable part of LLM-writes-Soar-rules: removing it cuts success by 23 (overall) and 37 (hard and variant) and pushes mean decision cycles above 1000x the minimum; removing the basic knowledge base costs 17 and the case base 14. Full framework: Gemini-2.5-Flash 86% and qwen-max 91% success, versus manual 84%, one-shot 55% and 66%, zero-shot 0% (N=100 Water Jug cases, single run, no intervals; the paper says 'reduction' without saying points or relative percent).
agent_test: Give the reviser the raw run trace (error, loop, cycle count) versus a summary; ablate the trace at equal tokens.

claim: A smaller model plus the closed generate-run-critique loop beat a larger model prompted one-shot (Flash 86% vs Pro one-shot 55% success). Authors call this preliminary; the loop's token cost is not reported, so an equal-token advantage is not shown.
agent_test: Match total tokens: small model with loop vs large model with k independent samples and a check.

claim: Tree of Thoughts, the closest published analogue of a tie-impasse lookahead, beat best-of-100 CoT on Game of 24 with GPT-4 (74% vs 49%; b=1 gives 45%) at about equal completion tokens (5.5k vs 6.7k per case) but higher dollar cost ($0.74 vs $0.47). On Mini Crosswords ToT got 60% word-level success and 4 of 20 games; removing backtracking dropped word success to 20%. Tasks were chosen so search helps; 20 games is small.
agent_test: Run propose-evaluate-select only on items where the plain pass rate is non-trivial; compare with best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Gating search on need saves most of its cost: a rule deciding when to branch cut tokens, calls and runtime by 75 to 85% with small accuracy loss on math (100 items per benchmark), but with a weak evaluator accuracy fell toward chain-of-thought (0.27 vs 0.39 on Math500). Read through a page fetch only.
agent_test: Compare impasse-gated branching with always-on branching at equal tokens; vary evaluator strength.

claim: In the ALFWorld setup Reflexion fires reflection from a hand-written counter (same action and response for more than 3 cycles, or over 30 actions); other tasks use LLM or test-based evaluation.
agent_test: Build S6 as typed trigger plus isolated subgoal plus stored fix, and ablate each of the three parts at equal tokens.
audit_note: Reflexion's repeat-counter heuristic (same action and response more than 3 cycles, or over 30 actions) is the hand-written ALFWorld trigger, one of two self-evaluation options (the other is LLM classification), not Reflexion's general trigger.
claim_before_audit: LLM agents rarely have a typed impasse. CoALA's cycle has propose, evaluate, select but no typed impasse or substate with typed result return; the Fan and Lan 2026 review of 42 systems finds the Soar bundle (typed impasse, isolated substate, compiled resolution) is not present as one package; Reflexion triggers reflection from a repeat counter (same action and response more than 3 times), not a typed impasse.

claim: No opened source tests whether typing the impasse (tie vs no-change vs conflict vs constraint-failure) changes outcomes for an LLM agent. Typed recovery is measured only for tool errors: PALADIN recovery 89.68% vs CRITIC 76.34% and vanilla 23.75% (Gemma-3 12B, own simulated benchmark, needs fine-tuning, GPT-5 as simulator and grader).
agent_test: Run the scaffold with one generic recovery operator vs impasse-typed operator choice at equal tokens. This is the central untested claim. Score typed operators by diagnosis accuracy (d02): the label only helps if it improves the diagnosis.

claim: Laird argues meta-reasoning needs no separate module because substate reasoning reuses the same decision cycle (contrast MIDCA, CLARION). This is a design argument with no head-to-head test in any source opened.
agent_test: Compare a recursive same-schema subgoal with a separate meta-prompt controller at equal tokens.

claim: Chunking has boundary conditions: it can cut steps while making total run time worse when learned rules are costly to match (expensive chunk problem, abstract level only), and the Soar 9.6 rewrite cut learned rules from 1263 to 8 for one arithmetic agent because old chunks were over-specific.
agent_test: Cap the size of the stored-fix library and test retrieval cost against token savings.

claim: A critical survey finds no clear success with prompted-LLM feedback outside tasks exceptionally suited to it; self-correction works where reliable external feedback exists.
agent_test: Measure diagnosis accuracy of each recovery operator against code-derived ground truth before comparing end accuracy.
audit_note: The Kamoi survey says prompted-LLM feedback succeeds only in exceptionally suited tasks and, separately, that self-correction works with reliable external feedback; the claim merges these into one condition.
claim_before_audit: The quality of the diagnosis is the bottleneck of generate-critique-repair loops. A stronger model's feedback beat both the baseline and own-feedback repair at every budget, human feedback raised GPT-4 repair success from 33.3% to 52.6%, and a critical survey finds success with prompted-LLM feedback only where external feedback is reliable.

claim: At matched sample budget, repair over resampling is conditional, not a reliable win. In code (Olausson) gains are modest or absent and more initial samples beat more repairs; on MATH (Snell) revisions narrowly beat parallel only with a fine-tuned revision model and a verifier, and a per-question mix saved up to 4x compute. Neither tests NL2GenSym or STARS.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: best-of-N plus code check, repair loop, and a mix. Report per difficulty bin.

claim: Earlier failed attempts in the context hurt later attempts. Lost-in-conversation: aptitude down 15%, unreliability up 112%, answers 20 to 300% longer as models lean on earlier wrong attempts, and restating facts recovers only 15 to 20% of the loss. Revision conditioned on past answers turned 38% of correct answers wrong (Snell). Both are non-agent settings.
agent_test: Run the same recovery step with the failed-attempt history in context versus a fresh context holding only a typed summary, at equal tokens.

claim: A separate subtask context that returns only a short result works in practice. Context-Folding (32K active window, 10 branches, no nesting) reached 62.0% and 58.0% after RL, above 327K ReAct; THREAD (prompt only) beat ReAct by large margins on ALFWorld (71.6 vs 20.1 with Llama-3-8b). Neither has an equal-token ablation, and the prompt-only folding agent did not match long-context ReAct.
agent_test: Isolation ablation: fresh typed-return subgoal vs shared context vs no subgoal, same total tokens.

claim: Code-fired stuck detectors are standard in agent frameworks. OpenHands fires on 4 identical action-observation pairs, 3 identical erroring actions, 3 repeated messages, a 6-step alternation, or 10 context condensations. No precision or recall is published, so our trigger thresholds cannot be justified from the literature.
agent_test: Log every trigger fire with a later-progress label to estimate false-alarm rate (stuck vs slow).

claim: Model-side signals of being stuck or of an unsolvable task are unreliable. Reasoning models spend 2x to 4x more tokens on missing-premise questions (over 3,000 vs about 1,000) and mostly fail to abstain; wrong answers show more thought switching than right ones (underthinking). This favours code-visible triggers and a budget cap over self-reported stuck.
agent_test: Compare code triggers against model-stated stuck on the same traces; add a seeded-contradiction set.

claim: Storing solved routines helps later tasks of the same kind but can be wrong. Agent Workflow Memory raised success by 24.6% (Mind2Web) and 51.1% (WebArena) relative and shortened runs; the authors say induced workflows can be incorrect and degrade results, and offline workflows can mismatch the test distribution. No token cost of retrieval is reported.
agent_test: Fix-library test: later items of the same class, accuracy and tokens including retrieval, with a size cap.

claim: Loop-like failures are common in LLM agent traces, but nobody counts Soar impasse types. MAST labels step repetition 15.7%, missed completion 12.4%, reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%, premature termination 6.2% and no or incomplete verification 8.2% in multi-agent frameworks. Tie and conflict are not categories.
agent_test: Count tie, no-change, conflict and constraint-failure events in our own scaffold logs on each benchmark.

claim: The right depth or token cap for subgoal recursion is unmeasured. Context-Folding forbids nesting and caps 10 branches; THREAD reached depth 10 with no cap tested; a 30K thinking-token cap with a forced best guess was reported slightly better than none in s1 (AIME24 N=30, caption only).
agent_test: Sweep depth cap 1, 2, 3 and token cap at equal total tokens; report variance over seeds.

claim: No replication, critique or independent follow-up of CogRec, NL2GenSym or STARS was found. The NL2GenSym citation list was empty and title searches returned only the originals; CogRec and STARS could not be checked (rate limits). This is weak evidence of absence.
agent_test: Treat all three as unreplicated; re-run a small version with seeds if any of their designs is adopted.
